# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 95 (Bi-Vb Pc95)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc95
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 95
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 95. Asking a question without permission
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc95
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 95, titled *Pañhāpucchana* ("Asking a question without permission"), establishes that a nun commits an offense requiring confession if she asks a monk a question without first obtaining leave [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. Like the immediately preceding rule (Pācittiya 94), this ordinance formalizes the subordination of nuns to monks and partially corresponds in content to the eighth *garudhamma* [Hüsken 1997].

The rule analysis outlines specific boundaries regarding permission: if a monk grants leave to ask about one branch of teaching—such as the Suttanta, the Vinaya, or the Abhidhamma—and the nun instead questions him about another, she incurs a pācittiya offense [Hüsken 1997]. This passage represents one of the few instances in the Vinaya where an explicit text called the Abhidhamma is presupposed, a fact that led Hermann Oldenberg to view the passage as an interpolation [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offense (*anāpatti*) provisions exempt a nun if she has obtained permission, including broad, open-ended leave (*anodissa okāsaṁ kārāpetvā*) allowing her to ask about any topic, as discussed also in the *Samantapāsādikā* [Hüsken 1997].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bi-pm-pc95*) and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, as well as Vinaya Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha counterparts across the Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions in Chinese, and the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 66 texts, most prominently with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 94 (§0.1–1.7) and Pācittiya 56 (§1.3–2.1.4) [DharmaNexus]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
